To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spatial layout in a virtual world can be used for structuring and visualizing a digital library.

(1) a virtual reality user interface can be generated automatically from an information retrieval system and that (2) the resulting user interface provides a spatial metaphor that highlights prominent structural patterns of the information retrieval system.
the spatial layout and the navigational structure of the virtual world highlight prominent structural patterns in digital libraries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing an intuitive and efficient virtual reality user interface for a digital library.
the development of a generic approach to augmenting user interfaces for large scale document collections.
the design of a generic framework for the development of user interfaces for digital collections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
virtual reality can provide an intuitive and powerful way of visualising and interacting with a digital library.
virtual reality is not yet a mature enough technology to be considered as a serious candidate for a user interface for a digital library.

the paper describes a very interesting approach to the development and implementation of a VR based user interface for digital libraries, but that there are some problems with the implementation and that some issues concerning the design and evaluation of the user interface have not been fully resolved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how the use of virtual reality can be integrated into the design of user interfaces for digital library systems.

the spatial layout and visualisation of a digital library in a virtual reality environment is a powerful tool for exploring the collection, for discovering and visualising relationships between documents and for browsing the library in a spatial context.
we have developed a virtual reality based interface that allows the user to explore a digital library in a natural way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
virtual reality can augment the user interface of a digital library by visualising the structural patterns in a collection of documents.
virtual reality can augment user interfaces for digital library systems and that the design and implementation of such interfaces can be automated to some extent.
the use of a virtual reality user interface for browsing and searching a digital library can be made more efficient by exploiting the structural properties of the digital library.
